subject: ela
intro: Authors write for a reason (their purpose) and often feel a certain way about their topic (their point of view). Read each short passage, then identify the author's purpose, the author's stance, or the word or detail that most clearly shows how the author feels. Watch for opinion words like should, must, best, and worst, and for loaded language that carries a positive or negative feeling.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

"Our school should add a recycling program right away. Every classroom throws away stacks of paper each day, and all of it ends up in a landfill. A few bins in every hallway would let us save thousands of sheets a year. The students are ready, and it is the right thing to do. We must act now."

What is the author's main purpose in writing this passage?
items.answer: The author's purpose is to persuade readers that the school should start a recycling program.

steps: Look for whether the author is just giving facts or trying to convince the reader of something.
The author uses opinion words like should and must and says it is the right thing to do.
The author also pushes the reader to act now, which is a call to action.
These choices show the purpose is to persuade readers to support a recycling program, not simply to inform.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

"Year-round school is a terrible idea. Families plan their whole year around summer break, and taking it away would wreck vacations and summer jobs. Students need a real rest, not a few short breaks scattered through the year. We should leave the school calendar exactly the way it is."

What is the author's point of view about year-round school?
items.answer: The author is against year-round school and thinks the calendar should stay the same.

steps: Point of view is how the author feels about the topic, not just what the topic is.
The author calls year-round school a terrible idea and says it would wreck vacations.
The author also states that the calendar should stay exactly the same.
These clues show the author opposes year-round school.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

"The city library is a wonderful place. Its shelves hold books on every subject you can imagine, and the reading rooms are quiet and welcoming. The friendly staff will help you find anything you need. Everyone in town is lucky to have such a treasure nearby."

Which word from the passage most clearly shows the author's positive feeling toward the library?
items.answer: The word "wonderful" most clearly shows the author's positive feeling.

steps: Loaded language is a word that carries a feeling, not just a fact.
Words like wonderful, welcoming, friendly, and treasure all show admiration.
Of these, wonderful is the strongest and clearest signal of a positive attitude.
It directly states how the author feels, so it best shows the author's positive stance.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

"A honeybee colony has three kinds of bees. The queen lays the eggs. Worker bees gather nectar and care for the young. Drones are male bees whose main job is to mate with a queen. Each type of bee has a role that keeps the hive running."

What is the author's main purpose in writing this passage?
items.answer: The author's purpose is to inform readers about the three kinds of bees in a honeybee colony.

steps: Check whether the author gives facts or tries to convince the reader of an opinion.
The passage only describes the queen, the workers, and the drones and what each one does.
There are no opinion words and no call to take action.
This means the author's purpose is to inform or explain, not to persuade.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

"Skipping breakfast is one of the worst ways to start your day. Students who skip it feel tired and have trouble paying attention in class. A simple meal in the morning gives you energy and helps your brain work. You should never leave the house without eating something first."

What is the author's point of view about eating breakfast?
items.answer: The author believes eating breakfast is important and that students should not skip it.

steps: Find how the author feels about the topic of breakfast.
The author calls skipping breakfast one of the worst ways to start the day.
The author also says you should never leave home without eating.
These opinion words show the author strongly supports eating breakfast.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

"Plastic straws are a careless waste. They are used for only a few minutes, yet they pollute oceans for hundreds of years. Sea turtles and other animals are harmed by them. Restaurants should switch to paper straws and help protect our oceans."

What is the author trying to get the reader to do or think?
items.answer: The author wants readers to believe plastic straws are harmful and that restaurants should switch to paper straws.

steps: Look for a goal the author wants the reader to accept or act on.
The author calls plastic straws a careless waste, which is loaded language showing disapproval.
The author says restaurants should switch to paper straws.
So the author wants the reader to agree that plastic straws are bad and support the change to paper straws.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

"Sea otters float on their backs at the surface of the water. They often wrap themselves in kelp so they do not drift away while they sleep. To open a clam, an otter places a rock on its chest and cracks the shell against it. These behaviors help otters survive in the ocean."

What is the author's main purpose in this passage?
items.answer: The author's purpose is to inform readers about how sea otters behave and survive.

steps: Decide if the author shares facts or argues an opinion.
The passage describes how otters float, sleep, and open clams.
There are no opinion words and no attempt to change the reader's mind.
The author's purpose is to inform readers about sea otter behavior.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

"The new parking lot is a reckless plan. It would tear out the only green space downtown, where families gather for the farmers market every week. Trading a beloved park for a slab of pavement is a mistake the city will regret. The council should reject this plan."

What is the author's point of view about the new parking lot?
items.answer: The author is opposed to the new parking lot and thinks it should be rejected.

steps: Point of view is the author's attitude toward the topic.
The author calls the plan reckless and a mistake the city will regret.
The author says the council should reject the plan.
These clues show the author is against building the parking lot.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

"School uniforms are a great idea. They make mornings easier because students do not have to decide what to wear. They also help everyone feel equal, no matter what their family can afford. Our school would be better off if every student wore a uniform."

Which sentence states the author's opinion most directly?
items.answer: "School uniforms are a great idea" states the author's opinion most directly.

steps: An opinion states a feeling or belief, while a fact can be checked.
The first sentence says uniforms are a great idea, which is a clear judgment.
Calling something a great idea shows how the author feels, not a fact.
So this sentence states the author's opinion most directly.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

"Volcanoes form where hot, melted rock rises from deep inside the Earth. When the pressure builds up, the rock bursts through an opening in the surface. The melted rock that flows out is called lava. As the lava cools, it hardens into new rock."

What is the author's main purpose in writing this passage?
items.answer: The author's purpose is to explain how volcanoes form and erupt.

steps: Check whether the author explains a process or argues for a side.
The passage describes step by step how melted rock rises and becomes lava and new rock.
There are no opinion words and nothing the author wants the reader to do.
This means the purpose is to explain or inform about how volcanoes form.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

"Homework should be cut way back. Students already spend seven hours a day in class, and piling on hours of homework leaves no time to rest or play. Kids learn better when they are not worn out. Teachers should give less homework so students can recharge."

What is the author's point of view about homework?
items.answer: The author believes students get too much homework and that teachers should give less.

steps: Find how the author feels about the topic of homework.
The author says homework should be cut way back and that teachers should give less.
These are opinion words that take a clear side.
So the author's point of view is that there is too much homework.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

"Adopting a shelter pet is the best choice you can make. Shelters are full of loving animals who need homes, and adopting one saves a life. The fees are low, and the staff help you find the right match. Choose adoption and give a deserving animal a second chance."

What is the author's main purpose in this passage?
items.answer: The author's purpose is to persuade readers to adopt a shelter pet.

steps: Look for whether the author informs or tries to convince the reader.
The author calls adoption the best choice and uses warm words like loving and deserving.
The author tells the reader to choose adoption and give an animal a second chance.
This call to act shows the purpose is to persuade readers to adopt a shelter pet.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

"Letting phones into classrooms is a dangerous mistake. They buzz and light up all day, pulling attention away from the lesson. Even one quick glance can make a student miss something important. Schools must keep phones out of class so learning can come first."

Which phrase shows the author's negative feeling about phones in class?
items.answer: The phrase "a dangerous mistake" shows the author's negative feeling about phones in class.

steps: Loaded language carries a feeling rather than a plain fact.
The author calls allowing phones a dangerous mistake.
The words dangerous and mistake both carry a negative feeling.
So this phrase most clearly shows the author's disapproval of phones in class.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

"A rainbow appears when sunlight passes through raindrops in the air. Each drop bends the light and splits it into different colors. That is why you often see a rainbow after a storm when the sun comes back out. The colors always appear in the same order."

What is the author's main purpose in writing this passage?
items.answer: The author's purpose is to explain how a rainbow forms.

steps: Decide whether the author shares facts or pushes an opinion.
The passage tells how sunlight passes through raindrops and splits into colors.
There are no opinion words and no call to action.
The author's purpose is to explain or inform about how rainbows form.

items.prompt:
Read the passage.

"Our town needs a new community pool more than anything else. Summers here are brutally hot, and there is nowhere safe for kids to cool off. A pool would give families a fun, healthy place to spend the day. The council should approve the pool this year."

What is the author's point of view about building a community pool?
items.answer: The author strongly supports building a new community pool.

steps: Point of view is the author's attitude toward the topic.
The author says the town needs a pool more than anything else.
The author calls a pool fun and healthy and says the council should approve it.
These clues show the author is in favor of building the pool.
